trade_source: drafting convention: a site plan in an electrical, mechanical, plumbing or telecom set (its sheet number's discipline or its title) is that trade's plan of the site, not a civil sheet
content_source: a site sheet carrying a trade's content (a luminaire type its fixture schedule lists, a panel circuit tag, a power or communications note) is that trade's plan of the site, whatever its discipline
building_source: drafting convention: a site plan draws the building's footprint (its layer named for the building when the set keeps layers); the site plan is laid onto the model by it
line_source: the plan's lines: a dashed line's dashes joined across gaps up to two text heights where they run on in one direction (up to ten where a label or a dot breaks the line and it runs on straight), on one layer; a line ending at two objects is the run drawn between them

register.source: the building outline the site plan draws, laid on the model's footprint: turned square to the model by its longest walls, the turn its walls' best fit, centred on the footprint; when the outline and the footprint differ in size the site plan is placed by its outline's centre and said so

equipment_source: the equipment a site plan's labels name, each a box where its symbol is drawn; its height the kind's usual one (a utility's pad-mount transformer, a monument sign) where no document gives it

pole.height_source: trade practice: a parking lot's area light on a 20 ft pole where its fixture schedule names a pole and no height (the schedule's height governs)
pole.size_source: trade practice: a 4 to 6 in square steel pole for a 12 to 30 ft area light (the pole's submittal governs)
pole.base_source: trade practice: a light pole's cast-in-place base, round, by the pole's height: up to 15 ft 18 in by 4 ft, up to 25 ft 24 in by 6 ft, taller 30 in by 8 ft, standing 24 to 30 in above grade in paving (the structural detail governs; each row: pole height ft, diameter in, depth in, above grade in)

trench_item: Trench, excavate and backfill (buried site conduit)
parallel_source: trade practice: a note's parallel conduits laid side by side in one trench, 2 in apart on spacers (NEC 300.5(I): a circuit's conductors together; the trench one for the set)
cover_source: NEC Table 300.5: rigid nonmetallic conduit 18 in cover, 24 in under parking lots and drives; a site run crosses paving, so 24 in
branch_conduit_source: trade practice: 1 in PVC the least below grade for a site branch circuit (NEC 352 permits 1/2 in; specifications and contractors bury 3/4 in to 1 in)
stub_source: rule: a buried run comes up 6 in above grade into the base or pad it feeds, the elbow and riser Sch 80 PVC (NEC 352.10(F))
primary_source: rule: a utility's primary called by a note with no line drawn runs out from the transformer away from the building to where the utility's line takes it; the utility locates it
site_load_source: a panel schedule circuit whose load is on the site (site and parking lighting, a monument or pylon sign, a gate, an EV charger) runs underground from the building to it
